answer: For each claimed identity, the node must complete a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings, where each result determines the next input; GPUs cannot shorten that chain by splitting its dependent steps across processors. An attacker can run clone chains in parallel only by provisioning additional resources, so the time-and-compute cost scales with identities. A Wesolowski proof lets verifiers check completion efficiently, turning the ridge between cheap cloning and costly participation into a crystal-clear barrier before dawn.
